summary: Builds the partnerships, funding and institutional infrastructure needed to create more student opportunities and make them accessible to students regardless of their ability to pay.
detailSummary:
King's already holds extensive relationships with employers, industry, public bodies, community and third-sector organisations, civic and cultural partners, international organisations and alumni. It also has staff capability, philanthropic relationships and multiple sources of financial support for student opportunity. These assets are distributed across faculties and professional services and are not yet consistently visible, coordinated or activated as a coherent institutional source of opportunity for students.

The proposition brings together three connected mechanisms. First, King's will strengthen the institutional infrastructure through which external relationships are understood, managed and converted into opportunity, including the role of alumni as partners, mentors, connectors and opportunity providers. Between October 2026 and April 2027, initial discovery will examine the current relationship landscape, staffing, systems, contracting, payments, partner experience and operational routes across faculties, SASD, IES and other relevant areas, and will return options for a stronger operating and investment model.

Second, over the same October 2026 to April 2027 period, King's will review and consolidate financial support for students undertaking employment-enhancing and developmental activity. The intended direction is a coherent Student Opportunities Fund combining low-friction microbursaries of around £150-£250 with more substantial awards of around £4,000 for genuine out-of-pocket participation costs. The fund should remove financial barriers to taking part rather than purchasing external courses or provision that King's could more appropriately provide through its own co-curricular and extracurricular offer.

Third, alumni engagement and philanthropy will be used deliberately to grow the supply of opportunity as well as access to it. Alongside philanthropic support for the Student Opportunities Fund, the proposition will develop funding models for service-learning and social-good projects. One model to explore is paid project-mobilisation roles for PhD students who originate and lead flexible projects with community or social benefit while creating meaningful participation opportunities for wider cohorts of students.

The causal logic is that King's can create substantially more accessible and meaningful student experience by connecting assets it already holds, strengthening the infrastructure that turns relationships into opportunities, and using philanthropic capital both to create opportunity and to remove barriers to participation. The enduring scale of that infrastructure must then respond to demand. In particular, 2.1.4 Curriculum-Embedded Opportunity Growth and Assurance and 2.2.4 Flexible Adjunct Experiential and Thematic Opportunities will create additional requirements for partner sourcing, relationship management, contracting, administration and opportunity brokerage. The operating model and resource requirement developed here must therefore be revisited as those propositions mature and as actual demand becomes visible.

caseForChange.problem: King's has substantial external relationships, alumni connection, staff capability and pockets of financial support for student opportunity, but these assets are distributed across organisational boundaries and are not yet consistently converted into a coherent supply of accessible student opportunities. Relationship management, staffing, systems, funding routes and philanthropic activity can operate separately, creating duplication, missed connections, uneven access and underused external capacity.
caseForChange.opportunity: King's can build a stronger institutional engine that connects relationship management, alumni engagement, philanthropy and student financial support. Better visibility and coordination of external relationships can increase the throughput and diversity of opportunities available to students. A consolidated Student Opportunities Fund can remove financial barriers to participation, while targeted philanthropy can create new opportunity supply, including service-learning and social-good projects mobilised by paid PhD student leads and opened to wider student participation.
caseForChange.whyNow: King's Edge is developing ambitious routes to grow experiential opportunity within the curriculum and across the wider co-curricular and extracurricular experience. That growth will increase demand for partnership sourcing, brokerage, contracting, administration and student financial support. A first-year institutional review provides the opportunity to understand and improve the existing asset base before significant growth is mobilised, while giving alumni engagement and philanthropy a clear strategic role in expanding both opportunity supply and access.
caseForChange.intendedChange: King's moves from fragmented relationship, opportunity and funding activity towards connected institutional infrastructure that can generate, broker and sustain high-quality opportunities at greater scale. External partners and alumni can engage through clearer routes; philanthropic capital is deliberately used both to expand opportunity and remove participation barriers; students can access more coherent financial support; and partnership capacity is periodically recalibrated against the demand generated by curricular and wider opportunity growth.
